title: Why the National Hurricane Center bet big on AI to forecast Isaias
key_facts: National Hurricane Center forecasters shaped their forecasts for Hurricane Isaias to closely match an AI hurricane model from Google DeepMind (WeatherNext 3).
From the first advisory on Tuesday the NHC forecast a Category 2 storm, while many physics-based models showed a weaker storm on a different track.
NHC director Michael Brennan said the AI models have shown more consistency from run to run.
Last year NHC forecasters, relying largely on DeepMind, predicted Hurricane Melissa would reach Category 5 almost three days before it hit Jamaica.
NHC partnered with Google to help train the model on its best-track data.
AI models are used alongside traditional physics models; Isaias is heading toward the northeastern Gulf Coast and had not yet made landfall.
quote_evidence: They shaped their predictions to closely match an AI hurricane model developed by Google DeepMind, rather than leaning on the classic physics-based models many Americans are more familiar with, such as the European and GFS.
If the forecast is accurate, it will mark a huge victory for Google and help the people in the path of the storm, who will have had more time to prepare for a significantly stronger blow.
why_it_matters_hint: Forecasters are now leaning on an AI model for a live storm, which gives people more warning if it is right.
event_date: Hurricane Isaias advisories from Tuesday 6 Oct 2026; CNN report 8 Oct 2026
notes: Outcome pending: landfall has not yet happened. Brennan said the AI is one tool among others.
